result:
Done. PR #144 is ready, green, and mergeable.

**What changed.** `arms.sh` labelled from whichever verdict was in its hand — `*PASS*)` → `verified`, `*FAIL*)` → `regressed`, unconditional, per verdict. The label is per-PR and the verdicts are per-prediction, so it reported the most recently judged *arm*. The label is now computed from every verdict on the PR's branch.

**The supersession rule: by issue number.** The newest registration for an issue counts, older ones don't; the PR is `regressed` if any issue's newest verdict is a FAIL. By-path was rejected for a concrete reason: a corrected prediction is a new sha and in practice a new name, so under by-path *no lane could ever clear a FAIL* — only someone with a shell on the host, and a cloud lane has no host disk. The case that would make by-path right (one issue, several independent claims that must hold at once, where a later PASS on one would silently bury a FAIL on the other) is named in `NOTES.md` along with the one line to change for it.

`ERROR` and `VERDICT: UNJUDGED` are not verdicts: they set no label and supersede nothing — otherwise an errored re-registration clears a regression it never measured, which is the original defect in a different hat.

**Explainability.** Each decision is written to `$WORK/arms/pairs/<sha>.label.md` as a table of every verdict and whether it counts, quoted into the `[job.arms]` comment with prose naming which verdict superseded which, and recomputable any time with `arms.sh state lane/<name>` (no device, no `gh`, no judging — which is also what makes it testable without a scored result directory). Cost is one pass over `pairs/` per tick, built once before the judge loop.

**Checks.** `selftest.sh`: 287 passed, 0 failed. The new fragment rebuilds PR #102's exact four verdicts and drives the judge loop through a stub `ab_compare.py` in a symlink tree. Against `origin/master`'s `arms.sh`, 17 of its 19 checks fail — and the first is a *negation* over `DELETE .../labels/regressed`, so a script that crashed would make it pass; it fails, which is the old code clearing #88's live regression. Nine of the 17 reds are one reason (the old file has no `state` mode), so the load-bearing falsifiers are the six end-to-end ones. The two that pass under the old code are right for the wrong reason there — they guard against fixing this into a label that never clears.

Two small things worth flagging: the first draft of the fragment expanded `$ARMS` inside `check … bash -c '…'`, where it is unset, so three checks ran `bash state lane/selftest`, read an empty script from stdin, and passed against anything — caught only because neighbouring checks in the same block failed and made me read it. And the branch is the PR's identity in this computation; if a lane branch ever carried two PRs over time, a verdict judged under the closed one would count toward the open one. Nothing on file does that, and it's recorded in `NOTES.md`.
